Location: joint activity design suggestions, route-puzzle and green-manufacturing workshop sections.
Status: a design proposal. Suggestions and intended evaluation outputs are not completed event results.

The proposal connects the team's straw-to-sugars-to-fermentation-to-PMA-to-material route with the partner's plant-to-product route. A classroom card puzzle asks learners to arrange each route, compare the steps, then choose how to use a new plant waste. Other proposed formats include a stakeholder hearing, a microbe job-matching game and a four-station escape challenge. The proposal recommends beginning with raw material, transformation and product rather than a long explanation of gene regulation. Suggested evaluation outputs include route explanations, decision reasons, questions, hints used and feedback for later revisions. It also outlines a 60-minute joint workshop.

Attribution: Heidelberg iGEM 2025; original page CC BY 4.0. This is a paraphrased source summary.

The team turned summer-school materials into an open learning platform combining illustrated protocols, calculators and module quizzes. They sought feedback from summer-school and school-workshop participants and subsequently added instructional laboratory videos. The platform serves advanced school students and undergraduates, both at home and alongside lab classes. For a classroom adaptation, short explanations, a worked example and an immediate quiz can accompany one selected task. This adaptation is our suggestion; the original report concerns Heidelberg's platform.

Location: Equ-Globalizing — activities for children with special educational needs.
Attribution: BUCT iGEM 2025; original page CC BY 4.0. This is a paraphrased source summary.

BUCT describes a two-day activity moving from illustrated explanations and drawings to colored-clay models of cells or engineered bacteria. Facilitators supported children individually and helped them translate drawings into models. The team collected teacher reflections and participant work as feedback. A shorter workshop could retain the drawing-to-model sequence, offer more than one way to respond, and ask facilitators to record where support was needed. Those changes are new planning suggestions, rather than outcomes reported by BUCT.
